content: 1. A 12-week randomized exploratory study was conducted to evaluate the early viral kinetics of telbivudine and entecavir in patients with HBeAg-positive chronic hepatitis B. 2. A 24-week, parallel-group, open-label, randomized clinical trial compared the early antiviral efficacy of telbivudine and entecavir in treating HBeAg-positive chronic hepatitis B virus infection in adult Chinese patients. 3. Long-term entecavir therapy has been shown to reverse fibrosis and cirrhosis while providing continued histological improvement in patients with chronic hepatitis B. 4. Entecavir treatment significantly reduces hepatic events and mortality in chronic hepatitis B patients with liver cirrhosis. 5. Long-term entecavir therapy decreases the incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma in patients with chronic hepatitis B. 6. The World Health Organization (WHO) has issued consolidated guidelines on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection, emphasizing a public health approach. 7. The long-term incidence of hepatitis B virus resistance to lamivudine in HIV-infected patients has been documented, highlighting the need for careful management. 8. Lamivudine resistance in immunocompetent chronic hepatitis B patients has been studied, revealing patterns and incidence rates. 9. Standardized nomenclature and assays for antiviral drug-resistant HBV have been established, along with recommendations for management. 10. Primary resistance, multidrug resistance, and cross-resistance pathways in HBV have been identified as consequences of treatment failure. 11. Virologic response and resistance to adefovir in chronic hepatitis B patients have been evaluated, providing insights into treatment outcomes. 12. The evolution of multidrug-resistant hepatitis B virus during sequential therapy has been studied, emphasizing the challenges of resistance management. 13. Long-term adefovir dipivoxil monotherapy has been assessed for up to five years in lamivudine-resistant chronic hepatitis B patients, demonstrating its clinical efficacy. 14. The long-term safety of lamivudine treatment in chronic hepatitis B patients has been established, with data supporting its use in advanced liver disease. 15. Mutations in hepatitis B virus resistant to lamivudine have been identified and characterized, providing a basis for understanding resistance mechanisms. 16. The dynamics of hepatitis B virus resistance to lamivudine have been studied, offering insights into the development and progression of resistance. 17. The Asian-Pacific consensus statement on the management of chronic hepatitis B has been updated, providing region-specific guidelines for treatment. 18. Recent data on the treatment of chronic hepatitis B with nucleos(t)ide analogues have been reviewed, highlighting advancements in therapy. 19. A two-year lamivudine treatment for HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B has been evaluated in a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. 20. Extended lamivudine treatment enhances HBeAg seroconversion rates in chronic hepatitis B patients, with results observed after three years of therapy. 21. Acute exacerbation and hepatitis B virus clearance have been reported following the emergence of YMDD motif mutations during lamivudine therapy. 22. The clearance of original YMDD motif mutants with the emergence of distinct lamivudine-resistant mutants has been observed during prolonged lamivudine therapy. 23. A systematic review and meta-analysis compared the efficacy of lamivudine plus adefovir versus entecavir in treating lamivudine-resistant chronic hepatitis B. 24. Entecavir plus adefovir has been evaluated in lamivudine-resistant chronic hepatitis B patients who failed lamivudine plus adefovir therapy. 25. Entecavir therapy has shown improved virologic, biochemical, and serologic outcomes in lamivudine-refractory chronic hepatitis B patients over 96 weeks. 26. Switching to entecavir in chronic hepatitis B patients with partial virologic response to lamivudine has been studied in a 96-week randomized trial. 27. A dose-ranging study of entecavir in lamivudine-refractory chronic hepatitis B patients has demonstrated its efficacy and tolerability. 28. The question of ALT flare during the switch to adefovir from lamivudine has been addressed in a single-center open-label, randomized safety study. 29. Adding adefovir to ongoing lamivudine therapy in chronic hepatitis B patients with YMDD mutant HBV has been evaluated for its clinical benefits. 30. Adefovir dipivoxil alone or in combination with lamivudine has been studied in lamivudine-resistant chronic hepatitis B patients, demonstrating its effectiveness. 31. Adding-on versus switching-to adefovir therapy in lamivudine-resistant HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B patients has been compared. 32. Adefovir plus lamivudine has been shown to be more effective than adefovir alone in lamivudine-resistant HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B patients over a four-year study. 33. Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) has been found to be an inadequate surrogate marker for detecting lamivudine resistance. 34. Updated definitions of healthy ranges for serum ALT levels have been proposed, emphasizing their clinical significance. 35. Factors related to post-treatment relapse in chronic hepatitis B patients who lost HBeAg after lamivudine therapy have been identified. 36. Determinants for sustained HBeAg response to lamivudine therapy have been studied, providing insights into long-term treatment outcomes. 37. The durability of serologic response after lamivudine treatment of chronic hepatitis B has been evaluated, highlighting its clinical implications. 38. The duration of lamivudine therapy for chronic hepatitis B has been studied, comparing cessation versus continuation after HBeAg seroconversion. 39. Sustained response after a two-year course of lamivudine treatment in HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B patients has been documented. 40. The clinical course of chronic hepatitis B patients who were off-treated after lamivudine therapy has been analyzed, providing data on relapse rates. 41. The durability of antiviral response in HBeAg-positive chronic hepatitis B patients who maintained virologic response for one year after lamivudine discontinuation has been assessed. 42. The question of whether lamivudine monotherapy should be stopped or continued in hepatitis B patients with favorable responses after more than five years of treatment has been addressed. 43. The durability of lamivudine-induced HBeAg seroconversion in chronic hepatitis B patients with acute exacerbation has been evaluated. 44. Lamivudine maintenance beyond one year after HBeAg seroconversion has been identified as a major factor for sustained virologic response in HBeAg-positive chronic hepatitis B. 45. Predictors of relapse in chronic hepatitis B after discontinuation of antiviral therapy have been identified, providing guidance for clinical management. 46. The clinical efficacy of a 24-month course of lamivudine therapy in HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B patients has been demonstrated in a long-term prospective study. 47. Long-term additional lamivudine therapy enhances the durability of lamivudine-induced HBeAg loss, as shown in a prospective study. 48. Long-term follow-up of patients with anti-HBe/HBV DNA-positive chronic hepatitis B treated for 12 months with lamivudine has been conducted. 49. HBeAg seroconversion after lamivudine therapy has been found to be not durable in chronic hepatitis B patients in Korea. 50. Stringent cessation criteria result in better durability of lamivudine treatment in HBeAg-positive chronic hepatitis B patients, as shown in a prospective clinical study. 51. Poor durability of lamivudine effectiveness has been observed despite stringent cessation criteria in HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B patients. 52. Virologic response to adefovir dipivoxil monotherapy has been found to be not durable in HBeAg-positive, lamivudine-resistant chronic hepatitis B patients. 53. Virologic response is not durable after adefovir discontinuation in lamivudine-resistant chronic hepatitis B patients. 54. Sustained responses and loss of HBsAg have been observed in HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B patients who stopped long-term treatment with adefovir. 55. Off-therapy durability of response to entecavir therapy in HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B patients has been evaluated.
